items.title: With 29-teams having played 4+ games, a stat we can start to trust is pace.
items.author: Hoop Informatics
items.body_excerpt:
With 29-teams having played 4+ games, a stat we can start to trust is pace. 

The below chart shows 
🔵 average second per possession on offense  
🟠 average second per possession on defense

left = faster
right = slower

Teams are organized by pace - possesions per 48 minutes (right column)

images.alt:
Dumbbell chart titled "Possession Length on Offense and Defense." It shows each NBA team's average possession length in seconds on offense (blue dot) and defense (orange dot) for the 2026-27 season to date. Teams are sorted by pace (possessions per 48 minutes), fastest at top. A dashed vertical line marks the league average of 14.1 seconds. Offense and defense values below are approximate readings from the chart.

Team (pace): Offense, Defense
Bulls (107.6): O 13.0, D 13.8
Bucks (106.2): O 13.1, D 14.1
Pelicans (104.8): O 13.9, D 13.6
Raptors (104.5): O 13.3, D 14.1
Heat (104.2): O 12.7, D 15.0
Kings (104.0): O 13.8, D 13.9
76ers (104.0): O 14.2, D 13.5
Nets (103.3): O 13.8, D 14.0
Pacers (103.0): O 13.5, D 14.4
Hawks (103.0): O 12.8, D 15.1
Timberwolves (102.5): O 14.6, D 13.5
Magic (102.2): O 14.1, D 13.9
Cavaliers (102.1): O 14.2, D 14.1
Trail Blazers (102.0): O 14.3, D 14.1
Warriors (101.6): O 14.5, D 13.9
Clippers (101.5): O 13.9, D 14.5
Jazz (101.3): O 14.7, D 13.8
Grizzlies (101.2): O 14.2, D 14.3
Wizards (100.8): O 14.2, D 14.3
Rockets (100.8): O 15.7, D 12.8
Lakers (100.6): O 14.6, D 14.0
Spurs (100.3): O 13.5, D 15.2
Mavericks (100.2): O 14.8, D 14.0
Celtics (99.7): O 14.4, D 14.4
Knicks (99.6): O 14.8, D 14.2
Nuggets (99.4): O 14.5, D 14.5
Thunder (99.0): O 14.6, D 14.5
Hornets (98.8): O 15.6, D 13.6
Pistons (98.0): O 15.0, D 14.4
Suns (98.0): O 14.1, D 15.0

The Heat have the fastest offense and the Rockets the slowest. The Rockets also show the widest gap, with the slowest offense but the fastest defensive possessions. The Celtics and Nuggets are nearly identical on both ends.

Data: Dunks & Threes. Viz: @Hoopinformatics.com on Bluesky.

quote.author: Hoop Informatics
quote.text:
With a majority of teams having played three games, it’s still too early to look at team stats as they are noisy and unreliable. 

In a couple days however, we will be able to analyze pace and 3pt attempt rate as after 4-games these stats pass the threshold where they become more real than noise.

images.alt:
Horizontal bar chart titled "# of Games Until We Can Trust Team Stats." A row of numbered circles across the top marks game numbers 1 through 30. Games 1 to 3 are shaded light purple and the rest dark purple. A dashed red vertical line runs down from game 3. Yellow bars show the game number at which each team stat becomes reliable, ordered from earliest to latest:

Pace: game 4
Three Point Attempt Rate: game 4
Free Throw Rate: game 5
Assist %: game 6
Opp 3pt Attempt Rate: game 7
Win %: game 8
Net Rating: game 8
Turnover %: game 10
Two Point %: game 11
Offensive Rebound %: game 11
True Shooting %: game 12
Offensive Rating: game 13
Opp Free Throw Rate: game 14
Defensive Rebound %: game 15
Opp Turnover %: game 15
Free Throw %: game 16
Defensive Rating: game 16
Three Point %: game 27

Footer: Via research by Krishna Narsu (@Knarsu3.bsky.social) posted to Nylon Calculus. Visual by Hoop Informatics.
